subject: Post-call: provisioning & scaling evaluation, SLO targets
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>
To: Ameera Qureshi <ameera.qureshi@healthgrid.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@healthgrid.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — provisioning, isolation needs, and SLOs

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap so we have shared alignment and clear next steps. I’ve kept this deliberately short.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Latency sensitivity: clinical triage use case needs median (p50) inference < 120 ms and p95 < 350 ms for 512-token requests (real-time assistant).
- Isolation & compliance: customer wants a VPC-deployed, customer-dedicated pool (no multi-tenant co-tenancy) and SOC2 evidence for data handling.
- Predictable cost & scale: initial throughput target ~600 qps daily bursts up to 1.2k qps; goal is capacity planning for Q3 ramp.

Redwood's preliminary recommendation (high-level)
- Dedicated pool: start with 8x A100 (80GB) equivalent reserved GPUs with autoscale headroom for 4 additional GPUs for burst.
- Deployment: Private VPC deployment (Dedicated mode) with private control plane; KV prefix caching and per-model quantized variant to lower per-token cost.
- SLOs: target 99.5% availability SLA for the dedicated pool and p95 latency under 350 ms for production route.

Open questions we asked (and items for follow-up)
- Can you confirm 99th percentile sequence length and typical prompt + response token distribution? (Carlos)
- Any internal procurement lead or security reviewer we should add to the thread for SOC2 evidence and contract redlines?

Attachments I’ll send after call:
- healthgrid-infra-scan.pdf (attestation of current infra constraints)
- mutual-action-plan-healthgrid.xlsx (draft MAP: milestones + procurement timeline)

Next steps (owners & timeline)
- Priya: upload MAP & infra scan (today) — action: review and comment (Ameera)
- Marissa: schedule a 30–45m technical deep-dive on model throughput/latency tuning next week — propose Wed/Thu 
- Rishi: provide preliminary cost modeling for the recommended 8+4 burst pool and SLO implications by EOD Fri.

If this aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive and attach the MAP.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan

Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — provisioning, isolation needs, and SLOs

Thanks Priya — clear and helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Token distribution: p50 ~ 220 tokens (prompt+response), p95 ~ 900 tokens (we occasionally hit long summaries). We'll extract a sample distribution file and upload it to the MAP.
2) Throughput: 600 qps is on average across our region; peak daily bursts align with business hours in US-EAST and are typically 09:00–12:00 ET.
3) Isolation: VPC + dedicated tenancy is a hard requirement for PHI ingest; SOC2 is required for procurement.

Procurement & legal: I’ve looped Carlos (IT procurement) for timelines and our security reviewer, Miguel (copied offline). Carlos — can you confirm target PO timelines and if we need an exec-level SOW?

I reviewed your recommendation quickly — 8 reserved GPUs + 4 burst looks sensible. Two asks for the tech deep-dive:
- Please include a short section on how KV caching will be surfaced to our app team and what TTLs we should expect.
- Can Marissa cover canary rollout/auto-fallback for model variants in case quantized variant shows quality drift?

I’ll review the MAP once received. Thanks — let us know Wed/Thu windows for the deep-dive.

Best,
Ameera
Ameera Qureshi

Thanks — quick procurement note from my side:
- We typically require SOC2 Type II attestation + product security questionnaire. Can you share Redwood’s latest SOC2 report and a completed security questionnaire template?
- Target PO lead time: 4–6 weeks after contract signature for capital allocation. If we can align a draft SOW and the MAP, we should be able to start internal approvals in that window.

On the MAP: would prefer the milestone list to include an explicit platform validation step (internal performance test with our 512/900 token traces) and a billing ramp clause for the first 60 days.

Carlos Vega
Procurement Manager | HealthGrid Inc.

2) Redwood architecture for Dedicated pools (Marissa) — VPC network layout, customer control plane, and isolation guarantees
3) Latency/throughput tuning (Marissa) — continuous batching, KV caching, and suggested config for p95 budgets
4) Canary + fallback policy (Marissa & Priya) — rollouts, quantized variants, and monitoring hooks
5) Procurement & next steps (Priya) — MAP review, SOC2 report delivery, and preliminary cost estimate timeline

I’ll attach a short ops playbook (2 pages) and a placeholder MAP row in the spreadsheet that outlines validation steps and billing ramp language.
